chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Part of the perfection of Hajj and 'Umrah is that you enter into the state of Ihram from the Miqat (stations of entering Ihram) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. Do not pass them unless you are in the state of Ihram. For he designated for the people of Iraq, and at that time Iraq was not [a specific place but referred to the region], the location of Batn al-'Uqayq from the side of the people of Iraq. And he designated for the people of Yemen, Dhat 'Irq (Yalamlam). And he designated for the people of Ta'if, Qarn al-Manazil. And he designated for the people of the Maghreb (West), al-Juhfa, which is Mahya'ah. And he designated for the people of Medina, Dhat al-Hulayfah. And whoever's residence is behind these Miqat stations, from the side facing Mecca, then his Miqat is his residence."
ai.seo_question: What are the designated Miqat stations for Hajj and 'Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific Miqat stations assigned by the Prophet Muhammad to various regions, reflecting the geographical and administrative divisions of the early Islamic community. It establishes the legal principle that residents living beyond these designated points must assume the status of Ihram from their own homes, ensuring the ritual purity and order of the pilgrimage. This narration underscores the importance of adhering to the Prophet's specific instructions regarding the sanctity of the Miqat boundaries.
